subject: Jonathan, son of Saul
note: Evidence for Jonathan's Bible figure page. Every quotation is in jonathan.quotes.json and passes verify-quotes.mjs. Fetched texts are in design/saints-hub/sources/people/jonathan/ (gitignored); the Fathers are the shared NPNF files. The Bible is the Berean Standard Bible (public domain); the chapters used are copied, verses joined, into bsb-jonathan-chapters.txt (1 Samuel 13, 14, 18, 19, 20, 23, 31; 2 Samuel 1, 4, 9, 21; 1 Chronicles 8, 10).

life.text: Saul chose 3,000 men; 1,000 were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin. Jonathan attacked the Philistine outpost at Geba; the news went out as 'Saul has attacked an outpost of the Philistines'. The Philistines came with troops 'as numerous as the sand on the seashore'; Israel hid in caves and cisterns. No blacksmith in Israel; only Saul and Jonathan had a sword or spear.

The climb at Michmash: Jonathan went with his armour-bearer without telling his father; cliffs Bozez and Seneh on either side of the pass; the sign ('Come on up'); he climbed on hands and feet; about twenty men struck down in about half an acre; the earth quaked and panic spread from God; 'So the LORD saved Israel that day'.
life.source: 1 Samuel 14:1-23 (BSB). The quiz's record cites 14:1 and 14:6.

life.text: Saul's oath against eating before evening; Jonathan had not heard it; he dipped his staff in the honeycomb and his eyes brightened; 'My father has brought trouble to the land'.

God did not answer Saul; Saul swore the guilty man would die 'even if it is my son Jonathan'; the lot fell on Jonathan; 'And now I must die?'; Saul swore again; the people said not a hair of his head would fall, and rescued him.

After David had spoken with Saul (after Goliath), the souls of Jonathan and David were knit together; Jonathan made a covenant with him and gave him his robe, tunic, sword, bow and belt (five things: the tile).

Saul ordered Jonathan and his servants to kill David; Jonathan warned David, pleaded with Saul ('The king should not sin against his servant David'), and Saul swore David would not die; then Saul threw his spear at David and David fled.

The New Moon feast: David's fear ('but a step between me and death'); 'Whatever you desire, I will do for you'; the covenant with the house of David (20:16); Saul's anger, his curse and his words about the son of Jesse; 'Why must he be put to death? What has he done?'; Saul hurled his spear at Jonathan; Jonathan left in fierce anger and ate nothing.

The arrows at the stone Ezel: the sign agreed (20:20 plans three arrows; 20:36 tells of an arrow shot beyond the boy, so the page says 'arrows' for the plan and 'an arrow' for the morning); the boy knew nothing; Jonathan gave the boy his equipment ('gear' on the page); David bowed three times; they kissed and wept, 'though David wept more'; 'Go in peace'.

At Horesh in the Wilderness of Ziph Jonathan strengthened David's hand in God, said David would be king and he second-in-command, and they made a covenant before the LORD. It is their last meeting in the text: Jonathan appears next at his death (1 Samuel 31).
life.source: 1 Samuel 23:14-18 (BSB); 1 Samuel 24 to 30 do not name him in company with David.

life.text: Three covenants with David: 18:3, 20:16 ('made a covenant with the house of David'), 23:18. The tile's 'Each one before the LORD': 20:8 calls the covenant 'before the LORD', 20:16-17 and 20:42 swear by the LORD, 23:18 'before the LORD'.
Saul accuses his servants of hiding that 'my own son had made a covenant with the son of Jesse'.

death.text: Killed with Abinadab and Malchishua on Mount Gilboa; Saul, wounded by archers, fell on his sword; 'So Saul, his three sons, his armor-bearer, and all his men died together that same day'. The bodies hung on the wall of Beth-shan; the men of valour of Jabesh-gilead marched all night, retrieved them, burned them, buried the bones under the tamarisk at Jabesh and fasted seven days.

David and his men tore their clothes, wept and fasted until evening for Saul and Jonathan; the lament (the Song of the Bow), taught to the sons of Judah, written in the Book of Jashar; 'How the mighty have fallen' three times (1:19, 25, 27); 'Tell it not in Gath'; 'the bow of Jonathan did not retreat'; 'I grieve for you, Jonathan, my brother'.

Mephibosheth was five when the report came from Jezreel; his nurse fled, he fell and became lame. David asked for anyone of Saul's house to show kindness 'for the sake of Jonathan', restored Saul's land to him and gave him a place at his table. David spared him from the Gibeonites 'because of the oath before the LORD between David and Jonathan'. David moved the bones of Saul and Jonathan from Jabesh to Zela, to the tomb of Kish.
death.source: 2 Samuel 4:4; 9:1-13; 21:7, 12-14 (BSB). Chronicles calls him Merib-baal: 1 Chronicles 8:34.

family.text: Sons of Saul: Jonathan, Ishvi, Malchishua; daughters Merab (firstborn) and Michal (the younger); wife Ahinoam; commander Abner. Chronicles: Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, Esh-baal. Ish-bosheth was forty when Abner made him king, and reigned two years. Michal married David and let him down from a window.
family.source: 1 Samuel 14:49-50; 18:27; 19:11-12; 2 Samuel 2:8-10; 1 Chronicles 8:33 (BSB). 'Eldest son' on the page: Jonathan is named first in every list, and the Orthodox Encyclopedia calls him Saul's eldest son (starshiy syn).

family.text: Chronicles traces Jonathan's line from Merib-baal through Micah, Ahaz, Jehoaddah, Zimri, Moza, Binea, Raphah, Eleasah and Azel, ending with the sons of Ulam (son of Azel's brother Eshek), 'mighty men of valor, archers'.

others.text: Mishnah, Avot: love that depends on a thing ceases when it ceases; the love of Amnon and Tamar against 'the love of David and Jonathan'. Taylor numbers the sayings 22 and 23 of chapter 5 (5:16 in most modern numberings).
others.source: Charles Taylor, Sayings of the Jewish Fathers (1897), chapter 5, at sacred-texts (taylor-sayings-jewish-fathers-ch5.txt).

others.text: Ambrose, On the Duties of the Clergy: Book 3, chapter 21 ('So it was with Jonathan...'); Book 1, chapter 32 (David 'agreed to the counsels of Jonathan, who was the younger'); Book 1, chapter 33 (Jonathan 'imitated the gentleness of holy David'); Book 1, chapter 40 (his courage as a young man); Book 2, chapter 7 (Saul's spear); Book 3, chapter 22 (friendship).

Chrysostom, Homily 7 on 2 Timothy: 'I will now cite you from the Scriptures a wonderful instance of friendship. Jonathan...'; he did not envy David, joined in obtaining the kingdom for him; 'Thus justice was conjoined with friendship.' Also Homily 33 on 1 Corinthians (Jonathan not ashamed of his friendship under Saul's insult) and Homily 14 On the Statues (the honey and the oath): not printed.
Josephus retells the honey: Jonathan 'was not dismayed at this threatening of death' and says 'Nor do I desire you, father, to spare me'.
others.source: Josephus, Antiquities of the Jews, book 6, chapter 6, tr. Whiston (josephus-antiquities-6.txt).

others.text: His name: Yehonathan, 'the LORD has given' (NAS Exhaustive Concordance); Brown-Driver-Briggs gives both Hebrew forms and the Greek Ionathan of the Septuagint.

saint.text: Not in the Roman Martyrology of 1916 (no Jonathan; 29 December is 'holy David, king and prophet'), nor in the 2004 Martyrologium Romanum (its index runs Iona, Ionatus: no Ionathas; David 'rex et propheta' is 29 December). Not in the USCCB 2026 calendar, the Church of England calendar, Lesser Feasts and Fasts 2022, the LCMS or ELCA calendars (the only Jonathans there are Jonathan Myrick Daniels and Jonathan Edwards), nor the Coptic calendar list on disk.
saint.source: shared/martyrology-1916.txt; people/jonathan/martrom2004.txt (archive.org OCR); shared calendar files.

saint.text: The Orthodox Encyclopedia (Pravoslavnaya Entsiklopediya, vol. 25, pp. 497-498) opens its article on Ionafan with no commemoration and no 'righteous' title, where it gives one for saints (its entry for Abel reads 'pam. v Nedeli sv. praotets i otets').
saint.source: pravenc-ionafan.txt (the free preview of the article).

saint.text: Wikipedia's infobox gives Jonathan 'Venerated in Roman Catholic Church, Eastern Orthodox Church; Feast December 29', with no source; its Eastern Orthodox 29 December page does not name him. Treated as a confusion with David's 29 December.

pictures.what: Frederic Leighton, Jonathan's Token to David, about 1868, oil on canvas, Minneapolis Institute of Art (74.71). Cropped to Jonathan's upper body (source x 450-2450, y 0-2100 of 3407x4655), 1714x1800.
The hub card, cut from the same Leighton (source 1120,131 to 1840,1031), 480x600, face centred, eyes at about 37%.
Cima da Conegliano, David and Jonathan, about 1505-10, oil on panel, National Gallery, London (NG2505). Cropped to the two figures' upper bodies; Goliath's head, lower left, is left out. 1452x1500.
Rembrandt, David and Jonathan, 1642, oil on oak, Hermitage. Detail of the embrace (Jonathan in the turban, per the Hermitage as cited by Wikipedia). 1200x1435. Gallery picture, wide screens only.

cut_for_space: Tidbit: was he older than David? Ambrose calls him 'the younger' (Duties, Book 1, chapter 32); but Ish-bosheth was forty at Saul's death (2 Samuel 2:10) and Jonathan is named first; David was thirty when king (2 Samuel 5:4).
Tidbit: the lament was written in the Book of Jashar, also named at Joshua 10:13.
could_not_verify: A day for Jonathan in any Orthodox menaion or synaxarion: none found (OCA, Greek and Russian sources not searched page by page); the Orthodox Encyclopedia's article gives none. Wikipedia's claim of 29 December is unsourced.
Whether David and Jonathan's love was romantic, a question many modern readers raise: deliberately not addressed on the page; flagged for the owner.
